Hi Lena / Marissa,

Thanks for the clear questions — below are our standard positions and proposed contract language. Happy to carve exceptions for enterprise deals with approvals; please flag any specific clauses you need tightened.

1) SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in production scope for our hosted offerings as of the latest audit (report available under NDA). If you need the report, we can provide it via an encrypted transfer once an NDA or DPA is in place. If you prefer interim evidence, we can share a control matrix and SOC readiness summary.

Proposed text: "Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report covering production inference and control environment within 10 business days upon execution of a mutually agreeable NDA/DPA."

2) Data deletion SLAs (primary customer data): Our standard deletion workflow for hosted accounts is to complete logical deletion of primary data within 5 business days of a valid deletion request and to remove the data from active stores. Physical/secondary deletion from backups follows the backup deletion workflow below. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can contractually agree shorter windows subject to operational controls.

Proposed text: "Redwood will logically delete customer primary data within five (5) business days of receipt of a valid deletion request. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to purge the data from backups and secondary storage in accordance with the backup retention schedule."

3) Logs and diagnostic artifacts: By default, system logs and diagnostic traces are retained for 90 days. We can offer configurable log retention down to 30 days for Enterprise customers on Dedicated or Private; shorter retention is available with an operational runbook and acceptance testing.

Proposed text: "System logs and diagnostic artifacts will be retained for a baseline of ninety (90) days. For Dedicated and Private deployments, Redwood will support configurable retention periods down to thirty (30) days upon customer request and contractual agreement."

4) Backups and immutable snapshots: Backups are maintained separately from active storage. Backups are not immutable forever; we use versioned backups with a retention period configurable per deployment tier. For hosted customers, the default backup retention is 90 days; we run periodic snapshot lifecycle policies and can schedule purge jobs. Deletion requests will trigger a workflow to mark data for removal and then execute backup purge jobs as allowed by snapshot retention windows. For strict immutability (e.g., legal hold scenarios) we treat snapshots as immutable for the hold duration; otherwise backups are rotative and purged according to retention.

Proposed text: "Backups are retained according to the agreed backup retention schedule (default: ninety (90) days for hosted). Redwood will mark deleted customer data and execute backup purge processes in accordance with the retention schedule. In the event of an agreed legal hold or immutability requirement, Redwood will preserve snapshots for the hold period."

5) KMS/HSM & HIPAA scope: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments via integrations with common KMS providers and HSMs. For hosted (multi-tenant) customers we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys; we can evaluate BYOK for hosted on a case-by-case basis for enterprise customers.

Proposed text: "Customer-managed key support (BYOK) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted multi-tenant customers, Redwood provides envelope encryption; BYOK may be made available subject to specific contractual and operational arrangements."
